# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi"))$reference`
* Description (clinical-covariate model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi"))$description`
* Description (radiomics substudy model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi_radiomics"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12983> (open access; PMC10431051)

Courlet and colleagues (2023) built a tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model
from real-world data: electronic health records and routine PET/CT or CT
images of 91 patients with advanced cutaneous melanoma who received
ipilimumab, nivolumab or pembrolizumab (alone or in combination) as first-line
therapy at the Lausanne University Hospital. Every malignant lesion was
segmented on every image and the lesion volumes were summed into a total
tumor burden (TTB, cm^3).

The total tumor burden `tumor_vol` obeys

`d/dt(tumor_vol) = kgrowth * tumor_vol - TRT_PHASE * kkill * tumor_vol`,
`tumor_vol(0) = TTB0`,

where `kgrowth` is an exponential growth rate fixed to a literature value,
`kkill` a log-kill rate shared by the three drugs, and `TRT_PHASE` the
paper's ON/OFF regressor (0 for baseline images, 1 from the start of
treatment onward, including after treatment discontinuation). The model has
no pharmacokinetics: a model in which the drug effect depended linearly on
dose fitted worse (Results, Base model).

The paper reports two final models, and both are packaged:

* `Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi` -- the model including clinical covariates
  (Table 2; n = 91). Serum albumin, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR)
  and ECOG > 0 act on TTB0, and NRAS mutation on `kgrowth`.
* `Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi_radiomics` -- the exploratory substudy model
  including PET radiomics features (Supplementary Material S5; n = 38). Two
  baseline texture features act on TTB0, and one baseline and two delta
  (first follow-up minus baseline) features on `kgrowth`.

The base models (Table 2 and Supplementary Material S5, without covariates)
are model-development steps and are not packaged; their omega values are used
below to check the variance-explained statements.

Because there is no drug input and no drug concentration, the PKNCA section
of a usual validation is replaced by checks against the closed-form solution,
the covariate effect sizes the paper reports (Figure 2 and Results) and the
variance-explained statements of the Results.

# Population

The clinical-covariate model was fitted to 311 TTB measurements (240 PET/CT,
71 CT) from 91 patients, a median of 3 per patient (range 2-10); baseline TTB
was missing for 27 patients (Results, Data). Table 1 of the paper describes
the cohort: 65% male, median age 68 years (IQR 60-76), median BMI 26 kg/m^2.
Treatments were ipilimumab + nivolumab (n = 20), ipilimumab + nivolumab then
nivolumab maintenance (n = 18), ipilimumab alone (n = 23), nivolumab alone
(n = 3) and pembrolizumab (n = 27). Median albumin was 42.5 g/L (IQR
40.0-45.0; 30% missing), median NLR 3.4 (IQR 2.4-4.3); ECOG was 0 / 1 / 2 / 4
/ missing in 51 / 18 / 4 / 1 / 17 patients; 34 tumors carried an NRAS mutation
(including 3 at an unknown position), 56 were wild type and 1 unknown.
Missing covariates were imputed to the median (continuous) or the most
frequent category (categorical).

The radiomics substudy model used the 38 patients of the PET/CT cohort with
radiomics features at baseline and first follow-up. The paper does not
tabulate their characteristics.

```{r load-models}
mod <- readModelDb("Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi")
mod_rad <- readModelDb("Courlet_2023_melanoma_ici_tgi_radiomics")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
ui_rad <- rxode2::rxode(mod_rad)
```

# Closed-form check of the ON/OFF structure

With the random effects set to zero, a patient whose treatment starts at day
`t_on` has `TTB = TTB0 * exp(kgrowth * t)` before `t_on` and
`TTB = TTB0 * exp(kgrowth * t_on) * exp((kgrowth - kkill) * (t - t_on))`
after it. The solve below starts treatment 30 days after the baseline image
(the paper accepted baseline images up to 3 months before treatment start)
and switches `TRT_PHASE` on through the time-varying covariate column. Both
sides use the same parameters, so the difference is pure integration error
and a tight bound is correct.

```{r closed-form}
t_on <- 30
cf_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 400, by = 5), t_on))),
  evid = 0L,
  cmt = "tumor_vol",
  ALB = 42,
  NLR = 3.14,
  ECOG_GE1 = 0L,
  TUM_NRAS_MUT = 0L
) |>
  mutate(TRT_PHASE = as.integer(time >= t_on))

cf_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui),
  events = cf_events,
  atol = 1e-12,
  rtol = 1e-10
) |>
  as.data.frame()

ttb0 <- exp(ui$theta[["lrbase"]])
kg <- exp(ui$theta[["lkgrowth"]])
kk <- exp(ui$theta[["lkkill"]])
cf_sim <- cf_sim |>
  mutate(
    closed = ifelse(
      time <= t_on,
      ttb0 * exp(kg * time),
      ttb0 * exp(kg * t_on) * exp((kg - kk) * (time - t_on))
    ),
    rel_err = abs(tumor_vol / closed - 1)
  )
max(cf_sim$rel_err)
stopifnot(max(cf_sim$rel_err) < 1e-6)
```

```{r closed-form-plot, fig.cap = "Typical TTB with treatment starting at day 30 (reference covariates: albumin 42 g/L, NLR 3.14, ECOG 0, NRAS wild type). Line: rxode2 solution; points: closed form."}
ggplot(cf_sim, aes(time, tumor_vol)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = closed), data = cf_sim[seq(1, nrow(cf_sim), by = 6), ], shape = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t_on, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time since baseline image (days)", y = "Total tumor burden (cm^3)")
```

For the typical patient `kgrowth` (0.0081/day) and `kkill` (0.008/day) almost
cancel, so the typical tumor burden is nearly flat on treatment; the response
heterogeneity of the cohort comes from the large IIV on `kkill` (CV 185%).

# Covariate effect sizes (Figure 2 and Results)

The Results report the median effect of each covariate on TTB0 at the 2.5th
and 97.5th percentiles of its distribution (Figure 2): +527% at albumin 30
g/L, -47% at 48 g/L, -50% at NLR 1.36, +116% at NLR 9.38, and +92% for
ECOG > 0, plus a 70% lower `kgrowth` for NRAS-mutated tumors. These numbers
are reproduced exactly when the reference patient carries the cohort medians
of Table 1 (albumin 42.5 g/L, NLR 3.4) rather than the normalization values
of the equation (42 and 3.14); the normalization constant cancels from such a
ratio, so the check below tests the exponents themselves.

```{r forest}
forest_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,
  time = 0,
  evid = 0L,
  cmt = "tumor_vol",
  ALB = c(42.5, 30, 48, 42.5, 42.5, 42.5),
  NLR = c(3.4, 3.4, 3.4, 1.36, 9.38, 3.4),
  ECOG_GE1 = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L),
  TUM_NRAS_MUT = 0L,
  TRT_PHASE = 1L
)
forest_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), events = forest_events) |>
  as.data.frame()
ref_ttb0 <- forest_sim$tumor_vol[forest_sim$id == 1]
forest_tab <- data.frame(
  covariate = c(
    "Albumin 30 g/L", "Albumin 48 g/L", "NLR 1.36", "NLR 9.38",
    "ECOG > 0"
  ),
  published = c(527, -47, -50, 116, 92),
  simulated = 100 * (forest_sim$tumor_vol[forest_sim$id != 1] / ref_ttb0 - 1)
)

nras_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2,
  time = 0,
  evid = 0L,
  cmt = "tumor_vol",
  ALB = 42.5,
  NLR = 3.4,
  ECOG_GE1 = 0L,
  TUM_NRAS_MUT = c(0L, 1L),
  TRT_PHASE = 0L
)
nras_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), events = nras_events) |>
  as.data.frame()
forest_tab <- rbind(
  forest_tab,
  data.frame(
    covariate = "NRAS mutated (effect on kgrowth)",
    published = -70,
    simulated = 100 * (nras_sim$kgrowth[2] / nras_sim$kgrowth[1] - 1)
  )
)

forest_tab |>
  mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Covariate value" = covariate,
    "Published change (%)" = published,
    "Packaged model change (%)" = simulated
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Change in TTB0 (or kgrowth) relative to a patient with albumin 42.5 g/L, NLR 3.4, ECOG 0 and NRAS wild type.")

# The paper rounds to whole percentages.
stopifnot(all(abs(forest_tab$simulated - forest_tab$published) < 1))
```

# Variance explained by the covariates

The paper states that the clinical covariates explained 24% and 16% of the
IIV on TTB0 and `kgrowth` (Results, Model evaluation), and that the radiomics
features explained 75% and 71% of the variability on TTB0 and `kgrowth` while
the variability on `kkill` increased by 35%. These statements hold for the
change in the SD of the random effect (omega), with omega derived from the
reported CV as `omega = sqrt(log(1 + CV^2))`; they do not hold if the reported
CV were read as `omega * 100` (TTB0: 38% instead of 24%). This is why the
packaged variances use `log(1 + CV^2)`.

```{r iiv-explained}
omega_from_cv <- function(cv) sqrt(log(1 + cv^2))
omega_pkg <- function(u, eta) sqrt(u$omega[eta, eta])

iiv_tab <- data.frame(
  model = c(rep("Clinical covariates", 2), rep("Radiomics substudy", 3)),
  parameter = c("TTB0", "kgrowth", "TTB0", "kgrowth", "kkill"),
  # Base-model CVs: Table 2 (base model) and Table S5 (substudy base model).
  base_cv = c(2.00, 0.59, 1.69, 0.39, 2.24),
  final_omega = c(
    omega_pkg(ui, "etalrbase"), omega_pkg(ui, "etalkgrowth"),
    omega_pkg(ui_rad, "etalrbase"), omega_pkg(ui_rad, "etalkgrowth"),
    omega_pkg(ui_rad, "etalkkill")
  ),
  published = c(-24, -16, -75, -71, 35)
) |>
  mutate(
    change = 100 * (final_omega / omega_from_cv(base_cv) - 1)
  )

iiv_tab |>
  mutate(change = round(change, 1), final_omega = signif(final_omega, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Base-model CV" = base_cv,
    "Final omega (packaged)" = final_omega,
    "Published change in IIV (%)" = published,
    "Change in omega (%)" = change
  ) |>
  kable()

stopifnot(all(abs(iiv_tab$change - iiv_tab$published) < 1))
```

# Virtual cohort and visual predictive check (Figure 3)

Figure 3 of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC of the clinical-covariate
model over 1100 days. The cohort below has 200 virtual patients with the
Table 1 covariate distributions: albumin normal with median 42.5 g/L and SD
3.7 g/L (from the IQR 40-45), NLR log-normal with median 3.4 and the IQR
2.4-4.3, ECOG > 0 in 23 of 91 patients (missing ECOG counted as 0, as in the
model), and NRAS mutation in 34 of 91. Treatment starts at the baseline image
(time 0) and `TRT_PHASE` stays 1 throughout, including after the last dose.

```{r vpc-cohort}
set.seed(20230612)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230612)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 42.5, 3.7), 25), 55),
  NLR = exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(3.4), (log(4.3) - log(2.4)) / 1.349)),
  ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 23 / 91),
  TUM_NRAS_MUT = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 34 / 91)
)
obs_times <- c(0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360, 450, 540, 720, 900, 1100)
vpc_events <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "tumor_vol", TRT_PHASE = 1L) |>
  arrange(id, time)

vpc_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, events = vpc_events, nStud = 1) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc_sum <- vpc_sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.10),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p90 = quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
kable(vpc_sum, digits = 3, caption = "Percentiles of simulated observed TTB (cm^3), 200 virtual patients.")
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Courlet 2023 (not prediction-corrected): 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of simulated TTB observations."}
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "red") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Total tumor burden (cm^3)")
```

The simulated median starts near 8 cm^3 and the 10th-90th percentile band
widens in both directions over time, driven by the large IIV on `kkill`, as
in Figure 3, where the observed median starts near 8 cm^3 and the prediction
intervals of the 10th and 90th percentiles spread over several orders of
magnitude after day 300. The paper's VPC is prediction
corrected, includes the observed covariates and imputes TTB = 0.001 cm^3
after a durable complete response, so only its central tendency is compared
here.

```{r vpc-check}
med0 <- vpc_sum$p50[vpc_sum$time == 0]
med0
# Figure 3: median of the prediction-corrected observations at day 0 is
# about 8 cm^3; a mis-transcribed TTB0 or covariate exponent moves it by a
# large factor.
stopifnot(med0 > 4, med0 < 16)
```

# Radiomics substudy model

The radiomics features enter as `exp(beta * feature / feature mean)`, so at
the substudy feature means every factor equals `exp(beta)`. The typical TTB0
at the means, `0.18 * exp(3.32 + 0.66)` = `r signif(0.18 * exp(3.32 + 0.66), 3)`
cm^3, is close to the TTB0 of the substudy base model (8.61 cm^3, Table S5),
and the typical `kgrowth` at the means is
`0.0081 * exp(-1.04 + 0.20 + 0.07)` =
`r signif(0.0081 * exp(-1.04 + 0.20 + 0.07), 3)` per day. The feature
distributions are shown only graphically (Supplementary Material S4), so the
simulation below uses the means and then moves one feature at a time.

```{r radiomics}
feat_mean <- c(
  RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_DEPENDENCE_ENTROPY_BL = 6.29,
  RADIOMIC_PET_GLRLM_GRAY_LEVEL_NONUNIFORMITY_BL = 74.87,
  RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_SMALL_DEPENDENCE_LOW_GRAY_LEVEL_EMPHASIS_BL = 0.013,
  RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_DEPENDENCE_ENTROPY_DELTA = 0.11,
  RADIOMIC_PET_SHAPE_ELONGATION_DELTA = -0.028
)
scen <- data.frame(
  scenario = c(
    "All features at their means",
    "Delta shape elongation 3x its mean (-0.084)",
    "Delta shape elongation 0 (no change in shape)"
  ),
  elong = c(-0.028, -0.084, 0)
)
rad_events <- tidyr::crossing(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(scen)), elong = scen$elong),
  time = seq(0, 720, by = 10)
) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "tumor_vol",
    TRT_PHASE = 1L,
    RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_DEPENDENCE_ENTROPY_BL = feat_mean[[1]],
    RADIOMIC_PET_GLRLM_GRAY_LEVEL_NONUNIFORMITY_BL = feat_mean[[2]],
    RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_SMALL_DEPENDENCE_LOW_GRAY_LEVEL_EMPHASIS_BL = feat_mean[[3]],
    RADIOMIC_PET_GLDM_DEPENDENCE_ENTROPY_DELTA = feat_mean[[4]],
    RADIOMIC_PET_SHAPE_ELONGATION_DELTA = elong
  ) |>
  select(-elong) |>
  arrange(id, time)
rad_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_rad), events = rad_events) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(scenario = scen$scenario[id])

rad_typ <- rad_sim |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  select(scenario, tumor_vol, kgrowth, kkill)
kable(rad_typ, digits = 4, caption = "Typical TTB0 (cm^3), kgrowth and kkill (1/day) of the radiomics model.")

# Every radiomics factor is exp(beta) at the feature means.
stopifnot(
  abs(rad_typ$tumor_vol[1] / (0.18 * exp(3.32 + 0.66)) - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(rad_typ$kgrowth[1] / (0.0081 * exp(-1.04 + 0.20 + 0.07)) - 1) < 1e-6,
  # A more negative delta elongation (a lesion becoming more elongated)
  # gives a higher kgrowth (Results, Radiomic features inclusion).
  rad_typ$kgrowth[2] > rad_typ$kgrowth[1],
  rad_typ$kgrowth[3] < rad_typ$kgrowth[1]
)
```

```{r radiomics-plot, fig.cap = "Typical TTB in the radiomics substudy model on continuous treatment, by delta shape elongation."}
ggplot(rad_sim, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Total tumor burden (cm^3)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate normalization values.** The packaged clinical-covariate model
  uses the normalization values printed in the Table 2 footnote equation,
  albumin 42 g/L and NLR 3.14. The Monolix project (Supplementary Material
  S7) normalizes to the weighted means 42.2266 g/L and 3.14052. With the
  printed values the predicted TTB0 is 2.8% lower for every patient
  (`(42.2266/42)^-5.27 = 0.972`); the NLR difference is negligible. The
  printed equation is followed because it is the published specification;
  a user who needs the fitted Monolix configuration can multiply TTB0 by
  `(42/42.2266)^-5.27`.
* **Missing covariates.** The Monolix project pools missing ECOG with ECOG 0
  and missing NRAS status with wild type, so a patient with unknown status
  should be given `ECOG_GE1 = 0` and `TUM_NRAS_MUT = 0`. Missing albumin and
  NLR were imputed to the cohort median in the paper.
* **NRAS mutations at an unknown position** count as mutated
  (`TUM_NRAS_MUT = 1`), per Supplementary Material S1.
* **Treatment regressor after discontinuation.** `TRT_PHASE` stays 1 after
  the last dose; the paper found that the same parameters described the
  tumor dynamics during and after treatment. Setting it back to 0 after
  discontinuation simulates a different model from the published one.
* **Time origin.** The Monolix model sets TTB(0) = TTB0 at the first record
  of each patient (the baseline image, kept with a missing value when the
  baseline TTB was missing); treatment can start later and is switched on
  through `TRT_PHASE`, carried forward from the preceding record as Monolix
  carries regressors. The simulations above start treatment at the baseline
  image except in the closed-form check.
* **kgrowth.** The fixed 0.0081/day follows Table 2. Supplementary Material
  S1 derives it by multiplying the linear (sum of longest diameters) growth
  rate of Chatterjee 2017 by 3 to convert it to a volume rate. The KL of the
  Chatterjee 2017 mixture model packaged in this library
  (`Chatterjee_2017_pembrolizumab_mixture`, 2.76e-3/day) would give
  0.0083/day; the packaged value is the paper's.
* **Saturation.** The Monolix model sets the derivative to 0 above 1e12 cm^3
  to avoid overflow; the packaged model keeps this guard. It is never reached
  at realistic tumor burdens.
* **Durable complete responders.** In the data, TTB after the first
  lesion-free image of a durable complete responder was removed and that
  image was imputed to 0.001 cm^3 (Supplementary Material S1). This is data
  handling, not part of the model.
* **Radiomics covariate form.** Supplementary Material S1 says the radiomics
  features were "centered on their mean" but writes the relationship as
  `(exp(RAD / RAD_mean))^beta`, and the Table S5 footnote equations divide by
  the means; the packaged model follows the equations. The feature means
  (6.29, 74.87, 0.013, 0.11, -0.028) are available only as these divisors.
  The radiomics features depend on the image processing (SUV map, 1 mm
  isotropic resampling, bin width 0.2, TTB-weighted aggregation over
  lesions); features computed with other settings are not interchangeable.
* **No PKNCA.** The model has no drug input or drug concentration, so a
  noncompartmental analysis does not apply.
* **IIV.** Both tables report omega as a CV of a log-normal parameter; the
  variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`, which reproduces the paper's
  variance-explained statements (see above). The omega matrices are
  diagonal, as in the Monolix project.
